industry: Med spas / aesthetics (injectables, laser, facials, body) and chiropractic
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'BOTOX' / 'Botox' unless the product is genuine AbbVie/Allergan BOTOX from authorized sources; use 'neuromodulator' or 'wrinkle-relaxing injections' otherwise (FDA warning letters; CDC counterfeit outbreak)

'FREE units of Botox', 'Buy 2 units get 1 FREE', 'FREE Botox with filler' (GOLD-med-spa-chiro-003/017/038): free/BOGO prescription-drug offers carry FTC Free Guide, state medical-board and (for beneficiaries) inducement risk; have the client's counsel approve
'FDA-approved' for off-label uses or for the spa itself; 'no risks', 'no downtime' without substantiation

'Look younger, live longer' (GOLD-med-spa-chiro-005) longevity claims; 'cures', 'fixes', 'corrects' for chiropractic; disease-treatment claims (e.g., headaches, sleep) without competent and reliable scientific evidence
'(a value of $250)' / 'reg. $450' unless that is the actual regular price (16 CFR 233) (GOLD-med-spa-chiro-002/054)
'Injured in an auto accident?' mail to accident-report lists in Florida within 60 days (FL 817.234); check other states
Before/after photos without authorization or comparable presentation; 'results not typical' disclaimers
Treatment-specific personalization on the outside of a postcard ('your last Botox')
compliance_notes: FDA/CDC (verified): FDA warning letter to Pure Indulgence Aesthetics (TX, 4/1/2026) found a med spa administered far more 'Botox' than it bought from AbbVie and held an unlabeled botulinum toxin vial (DSCSA violations). CDC/FDA 2024: 22 people in 11 states harmed by counterfeit or mishandled botulinum toxin, mostly given by unlicensed people or in non-healthcare settings. Implication for ads: use brand names only for genuine product; suspiciously low per-unit prices invite scrutiny; never imply a non-medical setting is fine.

Florida s. 456.062 (verified, 2026): ads for free/discounted services by physicians (ch. 458/459), chiropractors (ch. 460), nurses (ch. 464) and other listed licensees must print the 72-hour right-to-refuse statement in capitals. Non-licensee estheticians may not be covered; the client must confirm.

Florida s. 817.234 (verified, 2026 statutes): chiropractors (and others) may not solicit motor-vehicle-accident victims by direct mail within 60 days of the accident for tort/PIP claims; advertising to the general public is allowed. Other states have similar rules (not verified).
Medicare/Medicaid patients (OIG, verified): free exams/X-rays/gifts must fit nominal value ($15/item, $75/yr) or an exception; routine copay waivers and 'no out-of-pocket' ads are suspect.

HIPAA (verified): reactivation mail about the provider's own services to its own patients is allowed without authorization unless a third party pays for it; HIPAA applies if the practice is a covered entity. Keep treatment details off the outside of postcards either way.
Before/after and testimonials: 16 CFR 255 (typical-results rule); California BPC 651 (comparable images, named procedure, 'the same before and after results may not occur for all patients').
Gift cards (Reg E 12 CFR 1005.20, verified): purchased cards must stay valid at least 5 years; promotional/bonus cards are exempt only if they say 'promotional' on the front with expiry and fees.
Negative option/memberships: ROSCA online; state ARLs (e.g., CA 17602, AB 2863 from 7/1/2025); FTC click-to-cancel amendments vacated July 2025 (ANPRM March 2026).
State corporate-practice-of-medicine, supervision and delegation rules for injectables vary by state (not verified tonight); the client must confirm who may inject and who must be named in ads.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, relief are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold set's free/BOGO Botox units (GOLD-med-spa-chiro-003/017/038) and very low per-unit prices vs FDA/CDC counterfeit enforcement and state medical-board rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins. Offer $ off a treatment from a named licensed injector; use the BOTOX brand only for genuine product; free-unit offers only with counsel sign-off.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: MMR-041 chiro accident-list urgency ('LAST chance') vs relational tone and FL 817.234
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins on list timing (no FL direct mail within 60 days). Tone is the client's choice; both fear and relational are allowed when legal.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Pain-photo cliches (rendered spines, people clutching necks) vs sell-the-outcome rule
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Offer both: the client may use a pain image, but each combo includes an outcome photo option (activity regained). No votes yet to settle it.
